newsitem.title: GERMANY: D.Telekom weighs selling cable TV in bits. [CORRECTED 12:39 GMT 02/02]
newsitem.headline: D.Telekom weighs selling cable TV in bits. [CORRECTED 12:39 GMT 02/02]

text.p: Deutsche Telekom AG is studying whether to break its cable television network into regional companies, in which it would sell minority stakes, the weekly Der Spiegel reported.
The telecommunications giant still believes it should be able to hold on to the cable network, and could not be forced to sell it off, as some government officials in Bonn and Brussels advocate.
But it is looking into alternatives, the magazine said.
Economics Minister Guenter Rexrodt said earlier this week he was in favour of forcing Telekom to sell its cable network to promote competition.

A Telekom spokesman declined to comment on the specifics of the Spiegel report, but said the cable network is not up for discussion. "There is a lot of competition in cable-TV in Germany," the spokesman said.
Spiegel also reported Telekom plans to step up investment to expand the offering of broadcasting channels on its television cable to 150 from the current 30.
Telekom will invest one billion marks ($612.6 million) (corrects from 500 million marks) to complete the digitalisation of its network within two months, making the expansion possible, it said.
